itinerary_days.Day 3: Ngorongoro Crater:
After breakfast, continue your safari with a drive toward the Ngorongoro Crater, a natural wonder of the world. Formed about 2.5 million years ago, Ngorongoro is the result of a massive volcanic eruption that caused the collapse of a large volcano, creating the expansive and unbroken caldera we see today. This site is unique for its cohabitation of humans and wildlife, a phenomenon your experienced driver-guide will elaborate on during your visit.

​

Inside the crater, the abundant water supports a thriving population of over 25,000 large animals, including elephants, lions, leopards, hyenas, jackals, hippos, waterbucks, and baboons. With some luck, you may also catch a glimpse of the rare black rhino. After a day filled with exploration and incredible wildlife sightings, you will ascend from the crater and head to your next accommodation for the night.

itinerary_days.Day 4: Serengeti National Park:
Rise early for breakfast at your accommodation before departing with a packed lunch for Serengeti National Park, renowned for its expansive, open grasslands that provide excellent wildlife viewing opportunities. The park's climate and vegetation have remained largely untouched for millions of years, creating a pristine environment for numerous species.

​

Serengeti is celebrated not only for its diverse wildlife but also for the annual Great Migration. This spectacular event sees vast numbers of wildebeest, along with zebra and antelope, following a perennial journey in search of fresh pastures, dictated by the annual rainfall patterns.

​

After a comprehensive game drive exploring this iconic park, you will proceed to your accommodation for dinner and an overnight stay, reflecting on the day's adventures under the African sky.

itinerary_days.Day 5: Serengeti National Park:
An early morning game drive in Serengeti National Park is highly recommended today. For an extraordinary start, opt for a hot air balloon ride (additional charges apply). You'll be picked up from your lodge at 5:00 AM, with the balloon taking flight around 6:00 AM. From this unique vantage point, you'll witness the wildlife below as dawn breaks over the vast Serengeti. Upon landing, celebrate with a sumptuous breakfast accompanied by Champagne.

​

Following this memorable experience, your driver will pick you up to continue exploring Central Serengeti. Known as the heart of the park, this area is teeming with wildlife and is particularly rich in the habitats of the Big Five: elephants, lions, buffaloes, leopards, and the elusive black rhinos. Bird enthusiasts will also be delighted with the opportunity to spot over 500 bird species, including vultures, owls, bustards, cranes, and the impressive secretary birds. Dedicate your day to immersing yourself in one of the world's most renowned wildlife sanctuaries.

itinerary_days.Day 1: Arrival in Arusha:

This first day is designed for relaxation and acclimation, preparing you for the thrilling adventure ahead. If the weather is favorable, you'll be greeted by stunning views of Mount Meru and the majestic, often cloud-shrouded Mount Kilimanjaro.

While settling in, consider enhancing your stay with optional activities available in Arusha. Explore the serene Lake Duluti by canoe, discover local culture and sites on a city tour, unwind with a yoga class, delve into the aromatic world of a coffee tour, embark on scenic walking tours, or experience the landscape on horseback. itinerary_days.Day 3&4: Serengeti National Park:
The next two days are fully devoted to exploring the vast expanse of Serengeti National Park, a name derived from the Maasai word "Siringet," meaning "the endless plain." These days in the Serengeti promise unparalleled wildlife viewing opportunities, especially in the Central Serengeti, which is a hotbed for animal activity throughout the year.

​

In this heart of the Serengeti, you'll encounter a wide array of wildlife including elephants, giraffes, impalas, waterbucks, hippos, reedbucks, buffaloes, and baboons. These species thrive here year-round, well after the dramatic migration of blue wildebeest and zebras has passed through. The Serengeti is particularly famous for its high concentration of lions and leopards, making it a premier destination for big cat enthusiasts

.

Keep an eye out for the iconic Serengeti “Kopjes” – these striking granite boulders stand out against the grassy plains and serve as essential shelters for diverse flora and fauna. Each day, after immersing yourself in game drives and experiencing the wild beauty of the Serengeti, you will return to your camp to relax, dine, and rest under the stars, gearing up for another day of adventure in one of Africa’s most spectacular settings.

Although most of the campsites in the area are similar, it is one of few that are on level ground and well sheltered from winds, meaning less cold nights.

itinerary_days.Day 5: Ndutu Southern Serengeti Plains:
Start your day with a hearty breakfast before embarking on a full-day game drive in the Ndutu area. This region is known for its diverse ecosystems, including swamps, woodlands, and savannahs. With some luck, you may witness vast herds of wildebeest, zebra, and antelope stretching across the horizon. The hauntingly beautiful sound of wildebeest mooing adds to the day's unique experience.

​

February is a particularly special time in Ndutu, as many wildebeest give birth in a synchronized birthing event. The sparse grass offers little cover, making the newborns vulnerable to predators such as cheetahs, lions, hyenas, and leopards. Remarkably, wildebeest calves are able to run within minutes of birth, and by three days old, they are usually strong enough to keep up with the herd, adding a dramatic element to your safari adventure.

itinerary_days.Day 6: Ngorongoro Crater:
After breakfast, set off towards the Ngorongoro Crater, a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the most spectacular natural wonders in the world. Formed millions of years ago, the crater is home to over 25,000 animals, making it a high-density game viewing location.

 

As you explore the crater floor, you'll have the opportunity to see almost every species of East African savannah animal. The vast grasslands and acacia forests provide the perfect backdrop for spotting the "Big Five" (rhino, elephant, buffalo, lion, and leopard). Other residents include wildebeest, zebras, gazelles, and over 500 bird species. Keep an eye out for the endangered black rhino, a rare sight that may grace your visit if you’re fortunate.

itinerary_days.Day 7: Lake Manyara National Park:
At 8:30 AM, depart from your accommodation and head to Lake Manyara National Park, bringing along a picnic lunch for a full day of exploration. As you enter the park, you're welcomed by lush forests of Acacia and Mahogany trees, setting the scene for the day's adventure.

​

Spend the day immersed in a game drive that continues into the evening, breaking only for your picnic lunch. Keep an eye out for buffaloes, giraffes, impalas, baboons, and blue monkeys. One of Lake Manyara's highlights is its tree-climbing lions, although spotting them requires a bit of luck. In the right season, the lake's shoreline may turn pink with millions of flamingos—a breathtaking sight.

​

The day concludes with a drive back to Arusha, marking the end of your enriching 7-day safari experience with Mazingira Safari.

itinerary_days.Day 3: Lake Manyara & Masai Boma Visit:
After breakfast, embark on an early journey across the Great Rift Valley to Lake Manyara National Park. Though compact at 205 square miles, this park offers an array of stunning landscapes. Marvel at the lush acacia forests, giant fig trees, and mahogany canopies that shelter playful baboons and blue monkeys. As you explore, you'll encounter giraffes, elephants, impalas, and herds of buffaloes, while the lake itself is home to large numbers of hippos.

The game drives offer incredible photo opportunities, capturing giraffes and buffaloes set against the shimmering lake. After lunch, immerse yourself in the vibrant Maasai culture with a visit to a traditional Maasai boma. Learn about their marriage customs, culinary practices, and familial roles, and gain insights into their traditional medicine and fire-making techniques. End the visit with a lively Maasai dance before retiring to your lodge for a relaxed evening, dinner, and overnight stay.

itinerary_days.Day 6: Ngorongoro Crater:
Rise early for breakfast, then settle into your private safari vehicle for a scenic journey through the Great Rift Valley and crater forest, culminating at the breathtaking Ngorongoro Crater. As one of Africa's Seven Natural Wonders and its most-visited destination, the crater is home to an unmatched concentration of wildlife, including elephants, lions, buffaloes, hippos, and the elusive black rhino. itinerary_days.Day 3: Lake Manyara National Park:
AAfter breakfast, journey to the verdant landscapes of Lake Manyara National Park, a haven for birdwatchers. While the park offers exceptional bird photography and observation year-round, November to April is especially magical as it marks the arrival of migratory species from Europe and northern Africa. More than 400 bird species have been recorded here, and when water levels are ideal, thousands of flamingos blanket the lake in a mesmerizing pink hue, flocking to feed and breed. Spot distinctive species like the black heron, common little bee-eater, African grey hornbill, African fish eagle, and the striking yellow-billed stork. As you explore this ornithological paradise, you'll also encounter some of Tanzania's iconic wildlife, making it a day filled with wondrous discoveries both in the skies and on the ground.

itinerary_days.Day 4: Lake Natron:
Begin your day with a hearty breakfast before heading to Lake Natron, a thrilling destination for adventurers and a sanctuary for flamingos. While many creatures find the lake's saline environment inhospitable, the flamingos flourish here, feeding on its abundant algae. In September and October, thousands of these elegant birds gather to breed, creating a breathtaking spectacle. Alongside the flamingos, you'll also witness an array of fascinating bird species, including marabou storks, ostriches, kori bustards, secretary birds, and vultures. After breakfast, set out on a game drive to Serengeti National Park, where the boundless plains and teeming wildlife offer an unrivaled experience. The park's diverse landscape, from woodlands to riverine forests and grasslands, provides exceptional birdwatching opportunities. itinerary_days.Day 6: Serengeti National Park:
Spend another thrilling day in Serengeti National Park, chasing the elusive "Serengeti Specials"—birds endemic to this region and found nowhere else in the world. Among these rare species are the grey-throated spurfowl, Schalow's wheatear, red-throated tit, rufous-tailed weaver, grey-crested helmet shrike, and Schalow's turaco. You might also spot the secretary bird, African fish eagle, Fischer's lovebird, and numerous vulture species. Keep an eye out for the lilac-breasted roller, its vibrant plumage lighting up the trees alongside the road. After a day of unparalleled birdwatching, continue to the Ngorongoro Highlands for an overnight stay, ready for the next chapter of your journey.

itinerary_days.Day 7: Ngorongoro Crater:
BeRise early for breakfast before setting off on a journey through the Great Rift Valley's crater forests to reach the magnificent Ngorongoro Crater. As one of Africa’s Seven Natural Wonders and the continent's most visited destination, the crater is home to the densest concentration of wildlife in Africa, including elephants, lions, buffaloes, hippos, and the elusive black rhino. While the crater hosts the iconic Big Five, it's also a paradise for bird enthusiasts, boasting over 500 species. From a distance, admire flocks of pink flamingos gracing Lake Magadi, while ducks, herons, storks, and waders can be spotted up close. The grasslands reveal ostriches, kori bustards, grey crowned cranes, secretary birds, and rosy-throated longclaws, while the forests harbor Schalow's turaco, white-eyed slaty flycatchers, and an array of sunbirds. After this final day of exploration, return to Arusha for a transfer to the airport, concluding your unforgettable safari

itinerary_days.Day 1: Arrival in Arusha:
​

Upon landing at the airport, you'll be warmly welcomed by our representative and driven to your accommodation in Arusha, about an hour away. Your knowledgeable safari guide is a true expert on Tanzania, ready to share insights on the nation's vibrant culture, spectacular national parks, and diverse wildlife. Don't hesitate to ask questions along the way. If you arrive early, consider adding one of the following exciting activities: canoeing on Lake Duluti or Momela, exploring a local coffee plantation, taking a village or town tour, or another adventure of your choosing (for an additional fee). Settle in and prepare for an extraordinary safari experience that starts tomorrow.

itinerary_days.Day 2: Tarangire National Park:
​

Your personal driver-guide will pick you up from your Arusha lodge and guide you toward Tarangire National Park. As you pass through the Maasai plains dotted with acacia trees, you'll witness the Maasai herding cattle, riding bicycles, or guiding donkeys along the roadside. Tarangire is renowned as an elephant playground, home to large herds and countless other creatures like lions, zebras, wildebeest, buffalo, and warthogs, all visible from your open-roof safari vehicle. Look up into the trees, and you may catch sight of lions stalking their prey or leopards lounging above. During the dry season, the park comes alive as wildlife and birds flock to the Tarangire River, their lifeline. Return to camp for a delightful dinner and a restful overnight stay, dreaming of the adventures still to come.

itinerary_days.Day 3: Central Serengeti National Park:
​

After breakfast, set off for the iconic Serengeti National Park. The word "Serengeti" is derived from the Maasai term "Siringet," meaning "the endless plain," which perfectly describes the vast landscapes that await. The Central Serengeti is a wildlife paradise, offering year-round game viewing with a remarkable diversity of species. You'll encounter elephants, giraffes, impalas, waterbucks, hippos, reedbucks, buffaloes, and baboons, all residing in the area even after the dramatic herds of wildebeest and zebras have moved on.

After an exhilarating day of exploration, return to your lodge for a delicious dinner and a restful overnight stay, savoring the day's thrilling encounters with Tanzania's untamed wilderness.

itinerary_days.Day 4: Serengeti National Park:
​

Rise before dawn, ready to explore the Serengeti at its most captivating. The bush never sleeps, and early morning is when the wildlife action is at its peak. Predators rarely hunt in the heat, making the cool morning hours the best time to witness thrilling pursuits. Seronera, a year-round game viewing area, hosts a remarkable diversity of resident wildlife, including elephants, giraffes, impalas, waterbucks, hippos, reedbucks, buffaloes, and baboons. Despite the great migration moving on, you'll still find lions, leopards, and cheetahs during your day of exploration. After lunch, journey northwards for an unforgettable opportunity to witness the legendary Great Migration firsthand.

itinerary_days.Day 5: Northern Serengeti:
​

After breakfast, set out to fully embrace the magic of the Mara River. Explore both the northern and southern banks, anticipating the adrenaline-pumping moment of a wildebeest crossing. From July to October, the northern Serengeti plains are filled with massive herds, and you may witness thousands of wildebeest braving the river in search of greener pastures. This annual migration of over two million wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles across Northern Tanzania and Kenya is a breathtaking spectacle.

Savor the remarkable views of the southern Maasai Mara plains to the north and the brilliant sunset to the west. After a day of unforgettable wildlife encounters, relax over dinner before retiring for the night at your accommodation.

itinerary_days.Day 6: Northern Serengeti - Ngorongoro C:
​

After breakfast, set off on another exhilarating game drive through the northern Serengeti, where the Mara River flows. Here, you might witness hippos basking in the sun or submerged in the cool waters alongside massive crocodiles, both of whom call this river home. This region is alive with diverse wildlife—elephants, giraffes, and topi antelopes, while prides of lions and solitary leopards are often seen stalking prey across the rugged terrain.

 

After soaking up the northern Serengeti's wildlife spectacle, head toward the Ngorongoro Conservation Area.

Upon arriving at the crater's rim, you'll glimpse the marvels awaiting tomorrow: glistening streams, sweeping grasslands, and countless animals. For an unforgettable experience, consider adding an early morning balloon safari or a visit to Olduvai Gorge and its museum (optional activities with extra charges). Unwind in the evening over dinner at your accommodation, savoring the excitement for the adventures ahead.

itinerary_days.Day 6: Ngorongoro Crater:
​

After breakfast, descend to the floor of the renowned Ngorongoro Crater for a day of game viewing. The crater formed about 2.5 million years ago when a massive volcano collapsed inward, leaving the vast, intact caldera that we see today. This unique ecosystem is home to over 25,000 resident animals.

​

Visit Lake Magadi, a shallow alkaline lake in the southwestern corner, which attracts a large population of flamingos, hippos, and other waterbirds. The Big Five can also be spotted in the crater, adding to the day's excitement.

After an unforgettable day exploring this natural wonder, return to Arusha before heading to the airport for your departure or an extension to Zanzibar.

tours.name: 7-Day Kilimanjaro Expedition: Machame Route Adventure

itinerary_days.Day 1: Arusha - Machame Gate:
​

Day One of your journey begins after breakfast when your guide will collect you from your previous night's accommodation or Kilimanjaro Airport. From there, you'll drive to the Mount Kilimanjaro National Park gate, passing through the picturesque Machame village on the mountain's lower slopes.

​

After completing the necessary registration formalities, you'll start your ascent through the lush rainforest. The trail can be muddy and slippery, so be prepared as you navigate the terrain. By late afternoon, you'll reach Machame Camp, where you'll enjoy a well-earned rest, a hearty dinner, and your first overnight stay on Kilimanjaro.

Meal Plan

Breakfast, lunch and Dinner

Accomodation

Machame Camp -campsite is set in a small clearing in the forest, you will see a central ranger station and a number of brick toilets and long drop latrines. The air is quite humid 

Altitude 

3000m
itinerary_days.Day 3: Shira Camp journey to Laver Tower:
​

Start your day with a hearty breakfast at camp before continuing the ascent through the alpine desert toward Kibo Peak, where the western glaciers come into clear view. Pause for lunch at a picnic area before moving on to Barranco Camp. The Barranco Valley is one of the most picturesque areas along this trail, making this long hike an ideal acclimatisation day. Enjoy a well-deserved rest with an early dinner and overnight stay at camp.

Meal Plan

Breakfast, lunch and Dinner

Accomodation

Barranco Camp -
Perched at the head of a steep valley leading down to the Umbwe route and onward to Moshi, the camp sits beneath the dramatic cliffs of the summit massif. Here, you'll witness hanging glacier remnants and Kibo often cloaked in snow, while the valley below reveals the lights of Moshi. The campsite is equipped with brick toilets and latrines and a ranger's hut. It is full of  plant life, particularly the towering giant groundsels. 

Altitude 

 3900m
itinerary_days.Day 4: Barranco Camp Journey to Karanga:
Start the day by descending into a ravine at the base of the Great Barranco Wall. Climb this steep, non-technical cliff, which makes for a shorter hike ideal for acclimatization. You'll reach the next camp by late afternoon. The sunset here is stunning, offering breathtaking views of the southern glacier valleys and ice fields towering above. Enjoy a restful evening with an early dinner and an overnight stay at camp.

 

You'll have the chance to see giant groundsels and lobelias dotting the landscape, and perhaps spot rock hyraxes scurrying among the rocks. The views of towering ice fields and the valleys below provide a dramatic backdrop as you settle in for a night at camp.

Meal Plan

Breakfast, lunch and Dinner

Accomodation

Karanga Camp -
This camp is quite open and positioned on a slope, so ensure your tent is set up on level ground. The summit massif is visible with a clear view of the route to the top, and you can also see the lights of Moshi below. The camp is equipped with brick toilets, pit latrines, a ranger hut. Expect it to be windy and chilly, with fast-moving clouds. Water can be scarce here, as porters have to trek forty minutes down the trail to a stream. While many climbers skip Karanga to reach Barafu in one day, it's worth the stop for better acclimatisation.

Altitude 

 4000m
itinerary_days.Day 5: Katanga Camp, Journey to Barafu C:
​


After a satisfying breakfast, you'll depart your camp and head toward Barafu Camp, the base for your summit ascent. En route, you'll pass a junction linking with the Mweka Trail before continuing through rugged terrain to reach Barafu Hut. From this vantage point, you'll be treated to breathtaking views of both Mawenzi and Kibo peaks. An early dinner is arranged to ensure ample rest in preparation for your thrilling midnight summit attempt.

​

While at Barafu Camp, you'll likely witness stunning panoramic views of the glaciated Mawenzi and Kibo peaks, framed by the rugged alpine desert. As darkness falls, gaze up to marvel at the countless stars blanketing the night sky

Meal Plan

Breakfast, lunch and Dinner

Accomodation

Barafu Camp -Swahili word for "ice," this final camp sits at an elevation of 4,600 meters. While it no longer has permanent snow, it's still cold, rocky, and exposed. Altitude is noticeable here, and snow and wind are common. The campsites are tucked among the rocks along the ridge. Facilities include brick toilets and latrines, but water is scarce, requiring porters to make the trek downhill to the nearest stream. Rangers have robust stretchers with single wheels for quick evacuations, and there's a helipad nearby.

Altitude 

 4600m
itinerary_days.Day 5: Uhuru Peak, Journey to Mweka Camp:
​

You will wake up in the middle of the night for some snacks and hot tea or coffee, preparing to embark on the ascent guided by the light of your headlamp. By early morning, you'll reach Stella Point at the crater rim, where you'll pause briefly before continuing to Uhuru Peak. At Uhuru Peak, take in the breathtaking views and capture memorable photos at the summit before beginning your descent back to Barafu Camp for a short rest. Later, you'll continue down to Mweka Camp for your overnight stay.

​

Along the way, you'll experience the stunning sunrise over Africa, the glaciers glistening in the early morning light, and the expansive views of the plains far below. The descent will provide a unique perspective of the alpine desert zone and the transition back to lush, lower-altitude landscapes

Meal Plan

Breakfast, lunch and Dinner

Accomodation

Mweka Camp - Mweka Camp is strategically located on Mount Kilimanjaro's Mweka Route, serving as a primary descent campsite for climbers who have reached the summit via various routes. Situated at an altitude of approximately 3,100 meters (10,170 feet), it provides a much-needed resting point after the exhausting summit attempt

Altitude 

 3000m
itinerary_days.Day 5: Katanga Gate, Journey to Barafu C:
​

On the final day, after breakfast, you'll begin your trek down through the dense rainforest to the Mweka gate. Once there, you'll complete the final check-out formalities with the National Park. This is a great time for a heartfelt farewell with your crew before being transferred to your hotel. Here, you'll have a chance to freshen up with a shower and celebrate your achievement with well-deserved certificates.

​

As you celebrate your accomplishment, why not consider extending your adventure with a 3-day safari before heading home. Explore the breathtaking landscapes and incredible wildlife of Tanzania's national parks. We can arrange this on a per-person basis, giving you a chance to add an unforgettable safari experience to your journey.
